story.title: Apple Stores receive secret ‘Do Not Open’ boxes ahead of October 13 product launch - The Apple Post

facts.text: Apple retail stores received confidential boxes earlier this week featuring "Do Not Open Until October 8" stickers on them.
They are believed to contain new visual merchandise, which enables workers to update labels, graphics, and product layouts in stores around the release of new products.
If Apple announces the new devices sometime in the week of Monday, October 5, Apple Stores would need to update their displays for launch on October 13.

There is a possibility that the materials relate to the iPhone Duo , but it seems more likely given their confidentiality and timing that they relate to the rumored launch of Apple's smart home hub , alongside a new Apple TV 4K, and the HomePod mini 2.
Squarish 7-inch screen for controlling smart home products, listening to music, making video calls, and more.
MacRumors attracts a broad audience of both consumers and professionals interested in the latest technologies and products.
We also boast an active community focused on purchasing decisions and technical aspects of the iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other Apple platforms.
Get weekly top MacRumors stories in your inbox.
According to MacRumors , the boxes arrived at Apple retail stores earlier this week carrying “Do Not Open Until October 8” stickers.
The publication says it received a tip about the shipments and independently verified their existence.

The Apple Post reported yesterday that HomePad is expected to headline the October 13 announcements , giving Apple an entirely new product category built around the home and its next generation of Siri.
It does, however, provide another indication that something significant is happening in Apple’s retail operation ahead of the reported October 13 launch.
The company hasn’t confirmed what is inside the latest boxes, and there is no indication from the report that Apple Store employees have been given access to the contents ahead of October 8.
MacRumors says Apple Stores are preparing to begin installing the new product presentations from October 8.
Apple has yet to announce an October 13 event , despite the date now being linked to HomePad, HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K.
Retail merchandising can be prepared in advance of an announcement, particularly when stores need to coordinate changes across multiple locations.
